note: Hardcoded gap-check output for the scripted adult oncology visit (demo/onc_adult/script.json, 13 turns). Turn 11 ('Okay, okay') is a weak cue and is deliberately not flagged.

flags.rationale: The patient said he takes no blood thinners, but the chart lists warfarin.
The patient said his feet are fine, but the chart lists diabetic peripheral neuropathy. The treatment discussed can cause numbness in the feet.
The patient did not catch the part about the pump going home. The clinician did not repeat or explain it.

evidence.quote: I didn’t catch the last part.

flags.rationale: A multi-part plan (start date, infusion, blood draw, home pump, paperwork) was given and the patient was never asked to say it back.

evidence.quote: We plan to start in two weeks.

flags.rationale: Not covered: which signs, such as a fever, mean call the team or go to the emergency room, and the number to call.
Not covered: other options, a clinical trial, or a second opinion.
Not asked: what matters most to the patient, such as his work.
The clinician did not ask what the patient already knew or how much he wanted to hear before giving the results.
The patient asked whether he is going to die. The clinician moved on to treatment without responding to the worry.

evidence.quote: Am I going to die from this?

flags.rationale: His wife asked whether he can keep working. It was never answered.

evidence.quote: Will he still be able to work?

clarify: What fever or signs mean I call you, and what number do I use at night?
I asked if I am going to die. Can we talk about that?
Does a pump go home with me, and for how long?
